nodes.title: Ecology: Levels of Organization & Abiotic Factors
points: Ecology: Scientific study of interactions among organisms and between organisms and their abiotic (physical) environment.
4 Biological Levels of Organization: Organisms → Populations → Communities → Biomes.

Abiotic Factors: 1) Temperature: Most ecologically relevant; Eurythermal (tolerate wide range) vs Stenothermal (narrow range); 2) Water: Salinity levels (freshwater < 5 ppt, sea 30-35 ppt, hypersaline lagoons > 100 ppt); Euryhaline (wide salinity tolerance) vs Stenohaline (narrow tolerance); 3) Light: Photosynthesis, photoperiodism, animal diurnal/seasonal rhythms; 4) Soil: Soil texture, porosity, pH dictate vegetation.

formulas.label: Thermal & Salinity tolerance categories
formulas.expr: Eurythermal / Euryhaline: Wide range tolerance | Stenothermal / Stenohaline: Narrow range tolerance

formulas.label: Water salinity levels (ppt)
formulas.expr: Freshwater < 5 ppt | Sea water = 30 - 35 ppt | Hypersaline lagoons > 100 ppt

nodes.title: Responses to Abiotic Stress: Regulate, Conform, Migrate, Suspend
points: Homeostasis: Maintenance of constant internal body environment (thermoregulation, osmoregulation) despite ambient fluctuations.

1. Regulate: Maintain physiological homeostasis (mammals, birds). Energetically expensive; small animals (shrews, hummingbirds) lose heat fast due to large surface-to-volume ratio, hence absent in polar regions.
2. Conform: Internal state changes with ambient environment (~99% animals and all plants).
3. Migrate: Temporary escape in space to hospitable areas (Siberian cranes migrate to Keoladeo National Park in Bharatpur, Rajasthan).
4. Suspend: Escape in time: Hibernation (winter sleep in bears), Aestivation (summer sleep in snails/fish), Diapause (suspended development in zooplankton), Bacterial endospores, Seed dormancy.

formulas.label: Organismic responses classification
formulas.expr: Regulators (constant internal state) | Conformers (conform to ambient) | Migrators (escape in space) | Suspend (escape in time)

formulas.label: Suspension mechanisms matching
formulas.expr: Hibernation = Winter sleep (Bears) | Aestivation = Summer sleep (Snails) | Diapause = Zooplankton

nodes.title: Adaptations: Morphological, Physiological & Behavioral
points: 1. Desert Plants (Xerophytes): Thick waxy cuticle, sunken stomata, CAM pathway (stomata open at night), leaves modified into spines (Opuntia) with flattened green photosynthetic stem (phylloclade).
2. Desert Animals: Kangaroo rat in North American deserts never drinks water; meets 100% water demand from internal fat oxidation (metabolic water); excretes highly concentrated solid urine.
3. Allen's Rule: Mammals in colder climates have shorter ears and shorter limbs to minimize heat loss; seals possess thick subcutaneous blubber acting as thermal insulator.

4. Physiological Adaptations: Altitude Sickness at >3500 m (hypoxia causes nausea, fatigue); body adapts by: 1) Increasing RBC production; 2) Increasing breathing rate; 3) Decreasing hemoglobin-oxygen binding affinity.
5. Behavioral Adaptations: Desert lizards bask in sun to absorb heat when cold, and burrow underground when hot.

formulas.label: Allen's Rule statement
formulas.expr: Mammals from colder climates possess shorter ears and shorter limbs to minimize heat loss

formulas.label: Altitude sickness physiological adaptations
formulas.expr: Low pO₂ at high altitude → Body compensates: ↑ RBC count + ↑ Breathing rate + ↓ Hb-O₂ binding affinity

nodes.title: Population Attributes & Age Pyramids
points: Population: Group of individuals of the same species inhabiting a given geographic area, utilizing common resources, and interbreeding.

Population Attributes: 1) Birth rate (Natality): Number of births per individual per unit time; 2) Death rate (Mortality): Number of deaths per individual per time; 3) Sex ratio: Proportion of females to males.
Age Pyramids: Proportion of individuals across three age groups (Pre-reproductive, Reproductive, Post-reproductive):
- Triangular (Expanding population): Large base of pre-reproductive individuals (rapidly growing).
- Bell-shaped (Stable population): Pre-reproductive and reproductive individuals nearly equal.
- Urn-shaped (Declining population): Small pre-reproductive base, high older population.

formulas.label: Natality and Mortality rates calculation
formulas.expr: Birth Rate = Number of new births / Total initial population | Death Rate = Number of deaths / Total initial population

formulas.label: Age pyramid shapes and growth trends
formulas.expr: Triangular = Expanding / Growing | Bell-shaped = Stable | Urn-shaped = Declining

nodes.title: Population Growth Models: Exponential vs Logistic
points: Population Density (N): Dynamics governed by Natality (B), Mortality (D), Immigration (I), Emigration (E): N_(t+1) = N_t + [(B + I) − (D + E)].

1. Exponential Growth (J-shaped curve): Occurs when resources (food, space) are unlimited. Differential equation: dN/dt = rN (where r = intrinsic rate of natural increase). Integral form: N_t = N₀ e^(rt).
2. Logistic Growth (Verhulst-Pearl S-shaped / Sigmoid curve): Occurs when resources are limited. Incorporates Carrying Capacity (K: maximum sustainable population size).
Differential equation: dN/dt = rN [(K − N) / K]. Stages: Lag phase → Acceleration → Deceleration → Asymptote (at N = K, growth stops: dN/dt = 0). Represents realistic ecological growth.

formulas.label: Exponential growth equation (J-shaped)
formulas.expr: dN / dt = rN; N_t = N₀ e^(rt) (unlimited resources)

formulas.label: Verhulst-Pearl Logistic growth equation (S-shaped)
formulas.expr: dN / dt = rN [(K − N) / K] (where K = Carrying Capacity, r = intrinsic rate of increase)

nodes.title: Positive Population Interactions: Mutualism & Commensalism
points: 1. Mutualism (+ / +): Both species benefit obligately:
- Lichens: Fungus (absorbs water/minerals, protection) + Alga/Cyanobacteria (photosynthesizes).
- Mycorrhiza: Fungus (phosphorus absorption) + Plant roots (carbohydrates).
- Fig tree and pollinator Wasp: Co-evolution; wasp pollinates fig, fig provides oviposition site and food.
- Mediterranean Orchid (Ophrys) & Bee: Sexual Deceit (petal mimics female Colpa bee in shape, color, scent; male pseudocopulates achieving cross-pollination).
2. Commensalism (+ / 0): One benefits, other unaffected: Epiphytic orchid on mango tree; Barnacles on whale back; Cattle egret foraging near grazing livestock; Sea anemone and Clownfish.
3. Amensalism (− / 0): One harmed, other unaffected: Penicillium secreting penicillin inhibiting bacteria.

formulas.label: Population interaction signs summary
formulas.expr: Mutualism (+, +) | Commensalism (+, 0) | Amensalism (−, 0) | Predation (+, −) | Parasitism (+, −) | Competition (−, −)

formulas.label: Commensalism ecological pairings
formulas.expr: Orchid on Mango tree (+, 0) | Barnacle on Whale (+, 0) | Cattle Egret & Grazers (+, 0) | Clownfish & Sea Anemone (+, 0)

nodes.title: Negative Interactions: Predation, Parasitism & Competition
points: 1. Predation (+ / −): Predator captures and feeds on prey; energy transfer conduit; checks prey population (e.g. Prickly pear cactus in Australia controlled by Cactoblastis moth). Prey defenses: Camouflage, Monarch butterfly cardiac glycoside, Acacia spines, Calotropis cardiac poisons.

2. Parasitism (+ / −): Parasite lives on/in host for food/shelter. Ectoparasites (Lice, Ticks, Cuscuta); Endoparasites (Plasmodium, Liver fluke). Brood Parasitism: Cuckoo (Koel) lays eggs in Crow's nest.

3. Competition (− / −): Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle (two species competing for identical limiting resources cannot coexist indefinitely; inferior eliminated e.g. Abingdon tortoise in Galapagos extinct after goats introduced). Resource Partitioning (MacArthur: 5 Warbler species co-exist on same tree by foraging at different times/heights).

formulas.label: Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle
formulas.expr: Two species competing for identical limiting resources cannot coexist indefinitely; competitively inferior is eliminated

formulas.label: Brood parasitism pairing
formulas.expr: Koel (parasitic cuckoo) lays eggs in Crow's nest (eggs mimic crow eggs)

formulas.label: MacArthur resource partitioning
formulas.expr: 5 Warbler species co-exist on same spruce tree by feeding at different times and canopy zones

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Questions & Distinctions
points: Board Q1: Differentiate between Exponential growth (J-shaped) and Logistic growth (S-shaped) with graphical curves and mathematical equations.
Board Q2: Explain Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle with the example of Abingdon tortoise and goats.
Board Q3: Explain adaptations of desert animals (Kangaroo rat) and plants (Opuntia) to extreme arid environments.
Board Q4: Explain Mutualism with reference to: 1) Fig and Wasp co-evolution; 2) Sexual deceit in Ophrys orchid.
Board Q5: Differentiate between Hibernation and Aestivation.

formulas.label: Exponential vs Logistic differential equations
formulas.expr: Exponential: dN/dt = rN | Logistic: dN/dt = rN[(K − N) / K]

formulas.label: Intrinsic rate of natural increase (r)
formulas.expr: r = b − d (birth rate minus death rate; vital indicator of population biotic potential)

nodes.title: MHT-CET & NEET High-Speed Shortcuts & Traps
points: TRAP 1: Logistic growth equation: dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K]. When N = K, (K − N)/K = 0, so dN/dt = 0 (population stops growing, reaches carrying capacity asymptote).
TRAP 2: Predation vs Parasitism: Both are (+ / −), but a predator kills its prey immediately, whereas a parasite derives nourishment over time without killing host immediately.
TRAP 3: Brood parasitism: Cuckoo (Koel) and Crow is brood parasitism, NOT commensalism or mutualism!

TRAP 4: Allen's Rule vs Bergmann's Rule: Allen's rule applies to extremity lengths (shorter ears/limbs in cold climates); Bergmann's rule applies to overall body size (larger body size in colder climates).

TRAP 5: Small animals in polar regions: Shrews and hummingbirds are rare in polar regions because high surface area to volume ratio causes rapid heat loss, making thermoregulation energetically unfeasible.

formulas.label: Carrying Capacity asymptote trigger
formulas.expr: When Population N = Carrying Capacity K → (K − N) / K = 0 → Population Growth Rate dN/dt = 0

formulas.label: Ecological rules distinction
formulas.expr: Allen's Rule: Shorter ears & limbs in cold | Bergmann's Rule: Larger body mass in cold

nodes.title: Population Interaction Matrix & Calculation Hacks
points: Population Interaction Matrix: Mutualism (+, +); Commensalism (+, 0); Amensalism (−, 0); Predation (+, −); Parasitism (+, −); Competition (−, −).

Net population change calculation: If initial population N₀ = 1000, births = 200, deaths = 50, immigration = 30, emigration = 80: ΔN = (200 + 30) − (50 + 80) = 230 − 130 = +100 → New population = 1100.
Intrinsic rate of natural increase (r): For Norway rat = 0.015; Flour beetle = 0.12; Human population in India (1981) = 0.0205.

formulas.label: Complete ecological interaction matrix
formulas.expr: +/+ = Mutualism | -/- = Competition | +/- = Predation or Parasitism | +/0 = Commensalism | -/0 = Amensalism

formulas.label: Net population density change formula
formulas.expr: ΔN = (B + I) − (D + E)
